learning: Compare s-bend completion and max_error with iteration 1 (5/20, 0.0597 m). If the track is the lever, completion should rise. If steering_oscillation on the oval rises well above 0.30, the narrower track is adding jitter at this kp and kd.
notes: Builder's clean test: iteration 1 layout with wheel_track 0.10 m. kp scaled to 1.4 (about 0.10/0.12 of 1.6 plus a small margin) so that turn authority stays near the tested point. Everything else matches iteration 1.
rationale: Iteration 1 (score 482.7) is the best evidence: the oval finished 20/20, the s-bend 5/20, and the slalom 0/20. Every failure was an off-track end with max_error at or above 0.06 m, while rms_error stayed at 0.023 to 0.030 m. The limit is occasional large excursions on bends, not steady tracking error. The Builder's geometry is the iteration 1 layout with only wheel_track changed from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Turn rate scales as wheel-speed difference divided by track, so the narrower track gives about 1.2 times more yaw per turn unit. To keep the steering authority the same as the tested iteration 1 point, I scale kp by 0.10/0.12, giving kp of about 1.33. I use 1.4, which matches the value already run on a 0.10 m track in iteration 2 and leaves slightly more authority to counter the larger excursions. kd stays at 0.5 and ki at 0.05, as in iteration 1. base_speed stays at 1.0, which finished the oval with time to spare (1.69 s mean). The weights and last_direction line-loss recovery are unchanged. Expected result, as a hypothesis: s-bend completions at or above the iteration 1 rate, with max_error below 0.06 m on more runs. The risk is more oscillation at speed on the oval, which steering_oscillation will show. Because kp is scaled to offset the track's yaw gain, a flat score would mean the track effect is largely cancelled, so the Builder should read the race alongside the steering_oscillation and control_effort numbers.
